additional_concerns: The candidate leaves retention versus substantive fulfilment unresolved. Governance, supervisory conduct and operational results may provide different evidence; none is declared a universally sufficient test. Missing evidence must remain unresolved, and an operational failure alone does not establish loss of accountability.

Paragraph 14 most directly makes demonstration request-dependent while leaving confirmation untriggered. Footnote 5 repeats demonstration without that qualifier. Preserve this interpretive tension, the possible broader reach of the SFC-satisfaction and confidence standards, and the absence of a numerical confidence threshold.

Paragraph 15 concerns requested third-party audit or verification; paragraph 16 concerns a requested legal opinion. Neither supplies an automatic accountability test. Absence of a request does not extinguish continuing responsibility or the confirmation duty.

The two supplied versions of section 6.8 concern register maintenance, with the longer version adding requested address notification. Section 6.11C supplies a valuation-specific care and supervision standard, not a universal outsourcing safe harbour. Intermediary paragraph 13 has its own issuance and intended dealing or advising conditions.

Footnote 5 incorporates paragraphs 10–13, but the complete incorporated requirements are not supplied. Footnote 2 and the referenced Appendix Parts A and B are also absent. Obtain applicable missing material before asserting comprehensive fulfilment; no dependency identifiers are available.
